# Long-Term Fine Particulate Matter (PM2.5), Urban Heat Islands, and Incident Adult-Onset Asthma Across 14 Metropolitan Cohorts (2016–2025): A Synthetic Surveillance Study

Authors: Mateo Alvarez, ScD; Amina Darwish, PhD; Kenji Takahashi, MD, MPH

Affiliations: Global Environmental Epidemiology Consortium (SYNTHETIC DEMONSTRATION DATA)

## Background

Ambient PM2.5 and intensifying urban heat islands (UHI) co-occur in rapidly growing cities, yet synergistic effects on adult-onset asthma incidence remain poorly quantified.

## Methods

We linked 1-km satellite spatiotemporal PM2.5 and land-surface temperature anomalies to 218,400 asthma-free adults aged 25–74 followed over 1.84 million person-years (2016–2025).

## Results

Overall 8,912 incident asthma cases occurred (4.84 per 1,000 person-years). Each 10 ug/m3 higher 3-year rolling PM2.5 was associated with IRR 1.24 (95% CI 1.18–1.31, p = 0.0001); in high-UHI quartiles (+3.0 C anomaly), IRR reached 1.38 (95% CI 1.29–1.48; additive interaction RERI = 0.21, p = 0.003).

## Limitations

Residential address linkage did not capture occupational indoor filtration or commuting microenvironments.

## Conclusions

Combined PM2.5 reduction and urban tree-canopy cooling offer supra-additive potential for preventing adult-onset respiratory disease.
